why: The rule 'a file that returns a verdict must be able to fail' was scoped to the filename *_gate.py and every instrument written since was named lint_ or audit_, so the rule narrowed silently as the codebase grew. Widening the scope surfaced 45 at once. NOT A CLEARANCE -- each of these still cannot fail. THE COUNT MUST NOT RISE.
NOT_A_DEFECT_COUNT: 45 IS A READING LIST, NOT 45 BROKEN CHECKS. Some of these are reports BY DESIGN and belong in lint_gate_can_fail.KNOWN_TRIAGE with a written reason; some are genuinely vacuous -- a file that returns a verdict and can only ever pass. WHICH IS WHICH HAS NOT BEEN DETERMINED and nobody should quote 45 as a defect count, including us. The number that IS a finding is the difference: scoped to *_gate.py this rule saw about ten files and reported zero; scoped to the role it sees 163. The rule had been retiring itself as the codebase grew.
